title: Galaxy Z Fold8: Light, Cheap Android Alternative to iPhone Duo—Gizmodo Review
body:
Samsung has unveiled the Galaxy Z Fold 8, its eighth‑generation foldable smartphone, and the new device arrives with a strikingly lower price tag, a slimmer profile and a 4:3 aspect‑ratio display that Samsung says is optimized for video consumption. The move positions the Fold 8 as a direct competitor to Apple’s newly announced iPhone Duo, offering Android enthusiasts a premium foldable experience that can actually fit into a standard jeans pocket when closed.

The most noticeable change on the Fold 8 is the shift from the traditional 22:9 widescreen format to a more square‑ish 4:3 panel when the device is unfolded. Samsung’s engineering team explains that the new ratio delivers a cinema‑like viewing area that reduces letterboxing and makes movies, series and even gaming sessions feel more natural on a handheld screen. At 7.6 inches, the outer display remains a compact 6.2‑inch cover screen, but the hinge mechanism has been refined to reduce the device’s overall thickness by 0.5 mm, bringing the closed height down to 151 mm – roughly the width of a typical denim pocket.

Pricing is where the Fold 8 truly differentiates itself from Apple’s high‑end foldable offering. Samsung starts the base model at $1,199 for the 256 GB variant, a $800 drop from the iPhone Duo’s $1,999 launch price. The premium 512 GB version is listed at $1,399, still well under Apple’s entry‑level cost. Samsung attributes the reduction to economies of scale after eight generations of foldable production, as well as the use of a more cost‑effective Ultra‑Thin Glass (UTG) that still promises durability comparable to previous models. Early benchmarks from independent labs suggest the Fold 8 can survive over 200,000 folds without noticeable degradation, a figure that should ease lingering consumer concerns about the longevity of foldable screens.

Beyond hardware, Samsung is leveraging its software ecosystem to make the Fold 8 feel like a true multitasking powerhouse. The company’s One UI 6.0 now includes “Flex Mode Plus,” which automatically re‑arranges apps into side‑by‑side panes when the device is partially opened, and a new “Movie Mode” that adds cinematic letterboxing and adaptive brightness to enhance the 4:3 viewing experience. Samsung also promises an extended software support window of four years for Android updates and five years for security patches, a commitment that rivals Apple’s long‑term support and could sway enterprise buyers who have been hesitant about adopting foldables for work.

Analysts note that the Fold 8 arrives at a pivotal moment for the foldable market. Apple’s entry into the segment with the iPhone Duo generated a surge of media attention, but the steep price and relatively bulky design have limited its appeal to early adopters. Samsung’s strategy of incremental refinement—lighter chassis, more practical aspect ratios, and aggressive pricing—aims to broaden the foldable’s reach to mainstream consumers who want a larger screen without sacrificing portability. Market research firm IDC projects global foldable shipments to reach 25 million units in 2027, up from just 2 million this year, and Samsung’s price cut could accelerate that trajectory.

The Fold 8 also signals a shift in how manufacturers view the foldable form factor: no longer a novelty, but a viable alternative to traditional smartphones for media consumption and productivity. With the device’s improved ergonomics and more affordable price point, Samsung may have finally cracked the formula for mass‑market adoption. However, competition will intensify as other Android OEMs, such as Huawei and Oppo, prepare their own next‑generation foldables, and Apple is expected to iterate on the iPhone Duo later this year.

Looking ahead, the success of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 will likely hinge on consumer perception of durability, real‑world battery life and the ecosystem of accessories that can complement a foldable device. If Samsung can sustain its price advantage while delivering a reliable, high‑quality experience, the Fold 8 could set a new benchmark for the category and force rivals to rethink their own pricing and design strategies. The coming months will reveal whether the Fold 8’s blend of cinema‑grade viewing, pocketable size and competitive cost can truly reshape the foldable smartphone landscape.
